title: Eval signal throttler: Slack routing + PagerDuty ticket fingerprinting
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add an adaptive throttler and intelligent routing for evaluation regression signals in Console: (1) group/ fingerprint related alerts so Slack channels are not noisy, (2) deduplicate and fingerprint PagerDuty tickets to avoid ticket churn, (3) surface a clear per-alert provenance card tied to model/config changes and eval run snapshots.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows an 'Alert Fingerprint' for each eval-quality regression that is stable for >2 evaluation runs
Slack notifications are grouped by fingerprint and show a collapsed summary for repeated regressions within rolling 1h windows
PagerDuty integration creates at most one active incident per fingerprint per customer environment; subsequent signals attach to the existing incident and add context
Admins can configure suppression/backoff windows per project (0m, 5m, 1h, 6h) and a max-agg threshold that moves alerts to 'high-severity' routing
Dashboard exposes throttler metrics: grouped_alerts_count, deduped_pd_incidents, slack_collapses, false_positive_rate (estimated)
End-to-end test harness with synthetic eval regression sequences verifies dedupe behavior and routing policy (PR with test artifacts in GitHub)
Rollout feature flag exists: console.evals.alert-throttler with per-org opt-in
solution_summary: Implement a lightweight alert-fingerprinter service that computes stable hashes from eval signals (model version, config delta, evaluation suite, top failing prompts) and a routing policy engine that applies suppression and escalation. Extend Console notification templates to include a condensed history and action buttons (Acknowledge, Open PD, Suppress for X). Integrate with PagerDuty via fingerprint-aware incident creation and Slack via grouped message threads/attachments.
tech_notes: Fingerprint algorithm: stable concatenation of sorted keys (model_id, config_patch_hash, eval_suite_id, topN failing prompt hashes) then SHA256 truncate to 12 chars; include entropy threshold to avoid collisions

Routing engine: rule-set with conditions (customer_tier, severity_score, regression_rate) and actions (notify_slack, create_pd_incident, attach_to_pd, suppress) implemented as small DSL stored in Console DB
Telemetry: emit fingerprint_id, initial_signal_id, dedupe_action, pd_incident_id, slack_thread_ts as tags for downstream tracing
Backoff strategy: exponential backoff with jitter per fingerprint; also support sticky escalation that forces PD after N repeated signals within T minutes
Storage: short-lived KV (24h) for active fingerprints -> incident mapping; persistent index for last 90 days for audit and metric computation
Security: PD/Slack creds stored in KMS-backed secrets; permission check so only allowed org admins can change suppression policies
ux_notes: Console alert card should show: fingerprint summary (human-readable fields), last-seen time, occurrence count, linked eval snapshot (immutable), action buttons (ack/silence/escalate), and indication if this was caused by a model/config change. Provide an 'Investigate' shortcut that opens the eval diff viewer and pre-populates a new support ticket template.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: behind feature flag for internal Redwood orgs; run synthetic tests and smoke integration with internal PD/Slack
Phase 1: opt-in beta for 5 customer orgs with dedicated SRE/PM support; collect telemetry and refine fingerprint heuristics
Phase 2: gradual opt-in UI in Console for all orgs; default throttling conservative (longer suppression) and provide easy override
Phase 3: global enable and deprecation of legacy per-signal PD creation route after 2 weeks of stable metrics
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: over-aggressive dedupe may hide distinct regressions -> mitigation: include top failing prompt hashes and time-window sensitivity; expose 'force new incident' action
Risk: fingerprint collisions create false attachments -> mitigation: entropy threshold, collision monitoring alert and automatic fallback to conservative behavior
Risk: PD integration differences across customers -> mitigation: run pre-flight validation per org and fall back to creating new incidents if attach fails
Risk: Slack rate limits -> mitigation: batch grouped messages, use threads and message updates instead of new messages
